items.prompt: The cursor on Mrs Wati's laptop moves by itself and the antivirus is off. Put the steps in order.
steps: Disconnect the network (unplug the cable or turn off Wi-Fi)
Don't shut down the laptop or delete anything
Write down what you saw and what you tried
items.explanation: Disconnecting the network stops the attacker, and the traces on the laptop are important evidence. The SOC team investigates further.

items.prompt: You smell burning from a computer and see a little smoke. What do you do first?
choices: Restart it to see if it still works
Open the case while it's still on
Unplug the power and don't turn it on again
Keep working and report it tomorrow
items.explanation: Safety first: unplug the power so a fire doesn't start. Don't turn that device on again until it has been checked.

items.prompt: A disk is clicking and holds important financial reports with no backup. The decision?
choices: Keep trying to copy the data until it works
Escalate to the data recovery team
items.explanation: Don't experiment with important data on a dying disk. The data recovery team has special tools to save it.

items.prompt: Tap the signs that point to a possible attack.

parts.text: A strange program appears that the user never installed.
The screen is a bit dim because of battery saver mode.
Files in the work folder are suddenly locked and won't open.
The wireless mouse has a weak battery.

items.explanation: A strange program and suddenly locked files are signs of an attack, so escalate to the SOC. A dim screen and a weak mouse battery are normal.

items.prompt: A user can't hear any sound because the speaker is muted. Does this need escalation?
choices: Yes, every ticket must be escalated
No, just guide the user at the desk
items.explanation: Simple problems that can be solved at the desk don't need escalation. Unneeded escalation only keeps specialists busy.
